A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PriorDiffusion research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials are readable and support matching content across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot depth-estimation results on four benchmarks, training-convergence comparisons, qualitative examples, and prompt ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional denoising-step results, small-region evaluations, reconstruction examples, and a misleading-caption failure case.

M1.justification: The reported training-input procedure changes: v1 specifies LLaVA-Mistral with one caption-generation prompt; v2 specifies ten captions generated using Mistral and Vicuna with five prompts, randomly selecting one per training step. This is a limited training-pipeline adaptation. The depth architecture, frozen encoders, loss, and denoising equations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The two training datasets and four evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged. v2 adds a deliberately incorrect-caption inference scenario in Figure 9, replacing a bookshelf description with a window description. Its small-region and denoising-step evaluations otherwise reuse existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GeoWizard, Depth Anything, and Depth Anything v2 to the reported benchmark comparisons, substantially broadening the competitive context. The retained template-prompt experiment also gains a Marigold comparator row in v2 Table 5; v1 Table 2 contained only PriorDiffusion input variants.

E3.justification: v2 adds an inference sweep from 1 to 50 denoising steps and evaluation within MaskDINO regions occupying less than 5%, 10%, or 20% of NYUv2 images. It also revises caption preparation and corrects the stated training-normalization denominator. Dataset splits and the 30,000-iteration training budget remain unchanged. The formula correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis with denoising-step sensitivity tests, quantitative small-region evaluation, reconstruction error maps, and an incorrect-caption failure example. These investigate inference efficiency, local geometry, and susceptibility to misleading language. The existing prompt-generation ablation is retained, while the fixed-template study moves to Appendix C.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The ten training captions in v2 are input variants, not repeated experimental runs or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for new comparators, small regions, and denoising-step settings, and revises training-convergence curves. In Table 1, the 30,000-iteration PriorDiffusion row changes NYUv2 accuracy from 95.9% to 96.0%, KITTI accuracy from 90.6% to 90.3%, and ScanNet AbsRel from 6.8% to 6.7%. These are revised results alongside changed caption preparation, not established same-setting gains. Prompt-ablation Table 3 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Main-text Equation 1 changes the normalization denominator from y2 - y98 to y98 - y2, correcting the stated mapping to the intended range. However, v2 Appendix B.1 retains the old denominator in Equation 2. The diffusion mathematics otherwise remains unchanged; the evaluation formulas are relocated rather than newly derived.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes faster training convergence from faster inference and claims fewer inference denoising steps in the abstract, contributions, and conclusion. v1 discusses accelerated diffusion convergence but supports it through training-iteration comparisons. The central language-prior and user-directed depth-perception contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 reframes benchmark performance around training-data budgets, interprets language conditioning as a favorable initialization for denoising, and argues that language-conditioned training helps even with fixed inference prompts. The incorrect-caption limitation already existed and now receives an illustration. The earlier warning about diffusion's computational cost and suitability for resource-constrained deployment is removed.

D1.justification: v2 provides training-caption prompts and generation details, including 3.6 seconds per caption and 740 GPU hours for 740,000 captions on an RTX 3090. Table 1 adds comparator training-image counts and discloses evaluation without ensembling. The abstract promises code upon acceptance without providing access. v1's approximately four-day depth-model training estimate is removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands diffusion-depth discussion to GeoWizard, E2E FT, DepthFM, Lotus, and GenPercept, revises the description of Marigold, and removes four broader language-model references. The central novelty positioning remains. Depth Anything and Depth Anything v2 were already cited in v1; their updated publication metadata does not constitute new cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introductory passages are rewritten, related-work explanations are revised, and the experimental narrative is reorganized. Caption acquisition moves into Experiments, metric definitions and template-prompt discussion move to the supplement, and the conclusion and limitations exchange order. These are extensive structural changes beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds reconstruction, denoising-step, and failure-case figures plus small-region and step-sweep tables. Table 1 gains a training-image column and grouped comparator sections. The convergence chart is redrawn as adjacent panels, and the former main-text template table moves to the supplement and gains a comparator. Existing qualitative image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader baseline comparison, quantitative small-region analysis, and denoising-step study provide better checks on v1's accuracy and efficiency claims. Caption-generation details and costs improve reproducibility. The net gain is qualified by the unreconciled normalization formulas between the main text and appendix, and removal of the earlier computational-cost limitation despite newly disclosed substantial caption-preparation costs.
